summary: Klaus Karttunen specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (BA 1974, MA ~1977, Lic.Phil. ~1985, PhD ~1990) under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. His posts include acting professor (1982) and docent (1990) at Helsinki.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at the University of Halle and Goethe University Frankfurt (Dr. phil. 1954) under Paul Thieme. He was an assistant at the University of Göttingen (~1954–1957) and held an ordentliche Professur at Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at MLU Halle-Wittenberg (Diplom-Geograph 1961, Dr. phil. ~1964) and Leipzig (Habilitation 1968). He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1958–1964), Leipzig (1970–1991), Bayreuth (1990–1994), and Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg (under Spuler, Lentz, and von Gabain), and Giessen (Habilitation ~1971), later holding chairs at Giessen (1972) and Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Wille is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. His career includes attested appointments at the University of Göttingen (1996), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1997), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2020).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Klaus Sagaster, Michael Hahn (PhD, Marburg), and completed his habilitation at Hamburg (2004). He directed the NGMPP (1993) and served as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2012–2013).

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a Diplom in theology at Benediktbeuern (1971), a Doctor theologiae at the University of Munich (1984), and served as a Lehrbeauftragter at Munich in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Uppsala University by 2000, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1994), became Professor in the History of Religions at the University of Bergen (1996), and edited Brill's Encyclopedia of Hinduism (~2009).

Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao (MA ~1964), and Eihei-ji. He served at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center (1967–1970), Haiku Zendo (1970–1978), and taught regularly at Naropa University (2001).

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held several posts at Komazawa University, including head (学長, 1909), and was a special lecturer at the University of Tokyo.

Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's (~1958) and doctoral degree (1984) at Komazawa University. He spent his career teaching there as a professor from ~1965 to 2003.
Kodo Nomura was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a researcher (研究員) at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies master and scholar. He studied at Senju-ji, Takada Junior College, and Hōryū-ji under several teachers, later serving as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Koen Wellens specializes in Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar in Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at KU Leuven (~1980–1999) and also studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992).

Kogen Mizuno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. After earning a Doctorate of Letters at the University of Tokyo (1928), he became a professor at Tokyo (1959–1962) and served as professor and president (1976) at Komazawa University.

Kogi Kudara specialized in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He was a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and served in an editorial role for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He was attested as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima in 1991 and between 1997 and 2000.
